title: Artemis-Switch: a game streamed to your screen

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Your game runs on a powerful PC in another room, and the picture shows up on a handheld, smooth as if it were local. How?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's Artemis-Switch. It's a fork in the Moonlight streaming family, and Antoine's work sits on the graphics side.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the PC does the heavy lifting?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. The host runs the game. The client receives compressed video and audio, draws the frames, and sends controller input back.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And the point of the fork?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's a hardware-accelerated GameStream and Moonlight client written in C plus plus, with custom frame pacing for the Switch's display so video stays smooth, with no stutter. Antoine credits the upstream project, and the code is open under the GPL.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the clever bit is about when each frame hits the screen, not only how fast it arrives.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. A steady rhythm of frames feels better than raw speed. The written page has the full picture of the streaming path.
